content.text: Hi Aaron:  would you mind adding some more description to this issue?  Namely the steps (ideally in curl commands) to reproduce the issue.  That would be a big help to me.
Here are the steps I used (using the HTML UI, but it should be easily adaptable for curl):
Create a binary resource via PUT, e.g. at
/rest/resource1
Use a PATCH command to update the metadata at
/rest/resource1/fcr:metadata
PREFIX foaf: <
http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/
PREFIX dc: <
http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/
INSERT {
<> dc:creator <#creator> .
<#creator> foaf:name "Me" .
WHERE { }
I then see this error:

Unable to add child '#' with primary type 'nt:folder' to parent at /test2 with primary type 'nt:file' and mixins '{fedora:NonRdfSourceDescription,fedora:Resource}' in workspace 'default' of repository 'repo' because: - child's name '#' does not satisfy parent's child definition: nt:file/jcr:content (required primary types = [nt:base]) Unable to add child '#' with primary type 'nt:folder' to parent at /test2 with primary type 'nt:file' and mixins '{fedora:NonRdfSourceDescription,fedora:Resource}' in workspace 'default' of repository 'repo' because: - child's name '#' does not satisfy parent's child definition: nt:file/jcr:content (required primary types = [nt:base])

Just a note on this – the real problem here has to do with the way IdentifierConverters work and the way they are mapped to Modeshape resources. That's not to say that resolving this issue will necessarily involve rewriting the entire ID converter mechanism, but I suspect that it will not be trivial to fix.
This has not been resolved with api alignment.  Just a note.

I have a working implementation that allows hash resources to be added to binary resources. It creates a "#" node as an additional child of the nt:versionedFile that represents the binary. That is, it is a sibling to the "fedora:description" and "jcr:content" nodes.

Currently, I don't have any working integration tests. I've tried adding them to the FedoraBinaryImplIT class in the fcrepo-kernel-modeshape project, but it seems that creating the resource via the BinaryServiceImpl doesn't allow for the "#" node to be created. However, running HTTP requests to create and update a binary (as in the ticket description) do work.
Branch:
https://github.com/peichman-umd/fcrepo4/tree/FCREPO-1987
There has been additional discussion of this issue on Slack, and we haven't come to a resolution yet. Here are some of the issues:
The approach in this branch (
https://github.com/peichman-umd/fcrepo4/tree/FCREPO-1987

) makes the hash resources children of "#" node under the resource node that represents the binary. They are therefore not children of the "fedora:description" node. There was some concern expressed that this decouples these bits of the binary's metadata (those expressed using hash URI subjects) from the rest of the binary's metadata, especially with regard to metadata lifecycle and memento creation.

Changing the storage layout to make the hash URI tree a child of the "fedora:description" would require the HttpResourceConverter to be able to distinguish between the cases where "resource#hash" should become "resource/#/hash" (LDP-RS) and "resource/fedora:description/#/hash" (LDP-NR).
This could be addressed by making the hash URIs hang off of the "fcr:metadata" URI (resulting in URIs that look like
http://localhost:8080/rest/resource/fcr:metadata#hash

). This is currently not possible, as the repository rejects triples whose path does not match the path of the topic resource (a.k.a., the single subject restriction). Since /rest/resource/fcr:metadata is different from /rest/resource, this kind of update is currently not possible. If that restriction were loosened to allow triples with the same path but with an appended "/fcr:metadata", this should then be possible.

There may still be some issues in resolving the Modeshape nodes. Currently, when FedoraResourceImpl.updateProperties() calss getDescribedResource() to get the subject resource, if the request URI is a NonRdfSourceDescriptionImpl (as it is in the case of a PUT or PATCH to "resource/fcr:metadata", then it returns the binary resource itself (which will then resolve to the Modeshape path of "resource" and not "resource/fedora:description".

There is an additional tangential concern about allowing (or requiring) hash URIs hanging directly off of the binary URI, in that those hashes could interfere with the use of the hash portion of a URI to identify a document fragment. On the other hand, it is possible that we would want to allow such URIs as subjects, so you could provide metadata about specific portions of a binary.
Just a note that this is still an issue with commit
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/commit/7489ad5bc8fb44e2442c93eceb7d97ac54553ab6

> curl -i -ufedoraAdmin:fedoraAdmin -XPATCH -H"Content-type: application/sparql-update" -d "INSERT { <#part1> <http://www.purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/title> \"Some hash uri\" } WHERE {} " http://localhost:8080/rest/binary/fcr:metadata
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Date: Thu, 02 May 2019 16:23:30 GMT
Set-Cookie: JSESSIONID=1x0g02l7awrql4w6jb46tn573;Path=/
Expires: Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT
Set-Cookie: rememberMe=deleteMe; Path=/; Max-Age=0; Expires=Wed, 01-May-2019 16:23:30 GMT
Link: <http://localhost:8080/static/constraints/MalformedRdfException.rdf>; rel="http://www.w3.org/ns/ldp#constrainedBy"
Content-Type: text/plain;charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 225
Server: Jetty(9.3.25.v20180904)Unable to add child '#' with primary type 'nt:folder' to parent at /binary with primary type 'nt:versionFile' and mixins '{ldp:NonRDFSource,fedora:Resource,fedora:Binary}' in workspace 'default' of repository 'repo' because:
Closing due to general staleness, lack of relevance, or being no longer applicable.
It does not seem possible to create hash URIs on non-rdf source descriptions.
